Pousser un cri, pour le crapaud ou la grenouille

glosses: The vocal sound made by a frog or toad.

examples.text: Widow Toad: Looks kinds puny to me. Looks like a breeze could carry her off. Ribbit, ribbit. Maybe she could cook and clean my house.

Frogs croaking ribbit, ribbit
Trees rustling sssshh, ssshh
Water rushing over rapids splash, clash.

glosses: Used to anonymously and disrespectfully break silence, as in educational or ceremonial settings.

examples.text: The students fell momentarily silent while he finished writing on the board. Then, "Ribbit!"

glosses: The vocal sound made by a frog or toad.
To make the sound of a frog or toad.

translations.source_sense_description: Pousser un cri, pour le crapaud ou la grenouille

glosses: A faint, harsh sound made in the throat.
The call of a frog or toad.
The harsh call of various birds, such as the raven or corncrake, or other creatures.
To make a croak sound.
To utter in a low, hoarse voice.

examples.text: The raven himself is hoarse, / That croaks the fatal entrance of Duncan.

glosses: To make its vocal sound.
To die.
To kill someone or something.

examples.text: If Wilton croaked the criminal he did a jolly good day's work, and there's an end of it.
He'd seen my face, so I had to croak him.
"It was me. And I'm glad, damned glad, I didn't croak him. With this slick guy after me, it would be me for the chair."

glosses: To complain; especially, to grumble; to forebode evil; to utter complaints or forebodings habitually.

examples.text: Marat […] croaks with such reasonableness.

glosses: To abort the current program indicating a user or caller error.

examples.text: The accessor croaks if it's not an appropriate object reference.

translations.source_sense_description: Pousser un cri, pour le crapaud ou la grenouille

glosses: A shrill noise, especially made by a voice or bird. If made by a bird, it typically signals discomfort or anger; a yell, scream, or call.
A four-digit transponder code used by aircraft for identification or transmission of emergency signals.
A complaint or objection.

examples.text: That was the last roundup for McCutcheon’s Cresswell; it never moved from that field again. Not that there was any squawk from the landlord; the two of them owned it, of course.

glosses: An issue or complaint related to aircraft maintenance.

examples.text: We think instructors should stress the importance of writeups on all maintenance squawks after the completion of each flight. More important, something should be done by the aircraft operator to correct such squawks.

glosses: The American night heron.
A warning message indicating a possible error.

examples.text: The function-hiding code above, for instance, goes through a different (but widely used) compiler with nary a squawk.

glosses: To make a squawking noise; to yell, scream, or call out shrilly.

examples.text: The hens woke up squawking with terror because they had all dreamed simultaneously of hearing a gun go off in the distance.

glosses: To speak out; to protest.
To report an infraction; to rat on or tattle; to disclose a secret.

examples.text: "I'll slit your throat if you squawk on us," Krantz threatened.

glosses: To produce a warning message, indicating a possible error.

examples.text: That way, if you type = instead of ==, the compiler will squawk because you can't assign something to a constant.
You want the compiler to squawk if you try to instantiate for a type that doesn't implement IPrioritizable.

glosses: To set or transmit a four-digit transponder code. (Normally followed by the specific code in question.)

examples.text: After discovering that the hydraulic system is faulty, the pilots squawked 7700 and declared mayday.

glosses: To back out in a mean way.
